text:
[LGRA.23.2] **Residue the grammar does not carry ([STYL.2.15.4]).**

- **Modifiers are unordered.** A `kwarg_decl`'s modifiers may be written in any
  order; each may appear at most once, and the compiler must reject a repeated
  one (`DS_PARSE_KWARG_MODIFIER_DUPLICATE`).
- **Kwargs are unordered at the source and sorted in the artefact.** A
  service's `kwarg_decl`s may be written in any order. The compiler must emit
  them sorted by name, as it emits a call's kwargs ([RLOW.7.3.1]), so the
  artefact does not depend on the order the author wrote.
- **A `default` must fit the kwarg's declared type**, and the compiler must
  reject one that does not (`DS_VALIDATE_SERVICE_KWARG_DEFAULT_TYPE`):
  - a unit-typed kwarg takes a quantity in the unit's dimension. Where that
    dimension declares `storage int64` ([LUNI.7.2]), the quantity must also
    be a whole number of the kwarg's unit: `120 s` on a `min` kwarg is `2`,
    and `90 s` is refused;
  - a dimension-typed kwarg ([LUNI.7.1]) takes a quantity in that dimension;
  - an `Int`, `Float`, `String` or `Bool` kwarg takes a literal of its type,
    and a `Float` kwarg takes an `Int` literal too;
  - a kwarg of any other builtin type — `Bytes`, `Date`, `Duration`,
    `Interval`, `Json` or `Time` — takes no `default`;
  - a kwarg declared with a schema or with the kind `Schema` takes no
    `default` at all, because no literal has a schema type;
  - a kwarg declared with an opaque type takes no `default`, because no
    literal has an opaque type ([LOPQ.3.3]).

  A `-` before the literal is admitted only before a number or a unit
  literal. Before any other literal the compiler must reject it
  (`DS_VALIDATE_SERVICE_KWARG_DEFAULT_TYPE`). A negated unit literal has the
  value [LUNI.3.3] gives it: the literal's number is negated, then converted.

  What the service receives, from a `default` and from a written argument
  alike, is [LADP.8.5.2]. The meaning of `default`, and of `literal` and
  `required`, is [LADP.8.5.1].
- **`TYPE_SYM` in a `kwarg_decl` resolves in the type namespace** ([LGRA.22.7]):
  a scalar builtin, a unit symbol, a dimension or scalar-group name
  ([LUNI.7.1]), a schema, the kind `Schema`, or an opaque type ([LOPQ.3.2]),
  which an argument must match exactly. The compiler must refuse one
  that resolves to none of these, as it refuses a slot's
  (`DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_TYPE`, [LGRA.5.7.1]), and checks no `default` against
  it. A kwarg declared with a schema or with `Schema` takes only a pattern
  binding ([LADP.8.6.1]); the compiler must reject any other argument
  (`DS_VALIDATE_FACT_KWARG_NOT_BINDING`).
- **Every `service_decl` declares its response, as its last line.** The
  grammar makes `response_decl` required; the compiler must reject a
  declaration without one (`DS_VALIDATE_SERVICE_NO_RESPONSE_DECL`), naming the
  two forms. Its meaning is [LADP.8.4.2].
- **`TYPE_SYM` in a `response_decl` resolves to a schema**: a response is a
  fact, so a scalar, a unit symbol or the kind `Schema` there is a compile
  error (`DS_VALIDATE_SERVICE_RESPONSE_NOT_SCHEMA`). The schema it names must
  meet [LCRS.4.3.2].
